A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On the Convergence Rate of LoRA Gradient Descent. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original CIFAR-10 experiments with logistic regression and ResNet-18, including training-loss, parameter-norm, gradient-norm, and learning-rate curves.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds extended logistic-regression training, TinyLlama fine-tuning on Alpaca, and comparisons with full-rank training.

M1.justification: Equation (8) changes the prescribed theoretical learning-rate denominator from 5√2 L(...) to 4√2 L(...). Simultaneous LoRA updates and the practical adaptive and normalized learning-rate formulas remain unchanged; the new benchmarks do not introduce another algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 expands beyond CIFAR-10 image classification by fine-tuning TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 on Alpaca (Section 4, Figure 5). This adds language-model instruction fine-tuning to the retained image experiments.

E2.justification: v2 compares learning-rate schemes within LoRA. v3 adds full-rank training without LoRA as a central comparator for both logistic regression and ResNet-18 (Appendix B, Figures 7–8). The existing learning-rate comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 1,000-epoch logistic-regression run while retaining the original 60-epoch setting. Its new LLM experiments use rank 32, batch size 16, and initialization standard deviations 0.001 and 1/32; Figure 5 shows respective horizons of 500 and 250 steps with different constant-rate grids. Appendix B also introduces comparisons with and without LoRA.

E4.justification: New analyses investigate continued parameter growth after loss plateaus over 1,000 epochs (Figure 4), sensitivity to LLM initialization scale (Figure 5), and the effect of LoRA versus full-rank parametrization (Figures 7–8). These substantially extend the questions examined by v2's learning-rate studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Moving-average curves are retained as a presentation practice. The new Gaussian initialization standard deviation is an experimental setting, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original figure results are unchanged. Added results show continued logistic-regression parameter growth despite flattening loss, clearer learning-rate benefits under small LLM initialization than large initialization, and faster loss reduction without LoRA in the paired CIFAR-10 comparisons. These are new findings, not improved scores replacing v2 results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 restores a missing ||V1|| factor and revises Lemma 3.3's cubic terms. Lemma 3.4's descent decrement changes from ηt/5 to ηt/4, with corresponding proof constants updated and the old Equation (23) case analysis removed. The proof strategy, assumptions, and O(1/log T) and bounded-iterate O(1/T) rates remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement narrow convergence 'to a stationary point' to convergence of the minimum gradient norm; Theorem 3.5 still bounds the squared norm in both versions. The introduction also adds the qualification that learning-rate benefits depend on LLM initialization scale. The main novelty claim remains.

C2.justification: v3 interprets extended trajectories as evidence of unbounded logistic-regression iterates, stationarity at infinity, and asymptotic slowdown. It explains diminished LLM benefits through large, slowly changing parameter norms and softens the origin-based explanation of LoRA/full-rank differences. These materially expand the mechanism discussion and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: The anonymous code-access link is replaced by the named siqiaomu/lora GitHub repository. v3 supplies the LLM model, rank, batch size, and initialization scales, and explains that memory constraints exclude ηadapt from ResNet-18 testing. Table 1's original hyperparameters and the hardware/software disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds He et al. (2025) on subspace optimization and references for TinyLlama and Alpaca. It revises the attribution of boundedness assumptions, removing Sun et al. from that grouping while retaining its citation elsewhere, and shortens the characterization of Jiang et al. The broad research positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, related work, preliminaries, and discussion, plus a publication-footer update. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact. Added experimental passages and shortened mathematical derivations do not amount to a wholesale language or structural rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds multipanel displays for extended training, LLM initialization comparisons, and training with versus without LoRA (Figures 4–5 and 7–8). Original Figures 1–3 are unchanged, and v2 Figure 4 becomes Figure 6. Table 1 moves within Appendix B, while shortened reference-link labels compact the layout.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs the descent derivation and adds relevant LLM and full-rank comparisons absent from v2, improving rigor and empirical relevance. The initialization study also identifies a useful boundary on the schedules' benefits. However, finite training curves do not establish the new claims of unbounded iterates or slower asymptotic convergence, limiting the strength of the overall improvement.
